newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar steadies after erasing earlier gains.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steadies after erasing earlier gains.

text.p: 0138 GMT --*Dollar stable against yen in mid-morning Tokyo after erasing earlier gains due to selling from various operators, including overseas hedge funds, Japanese exporters and Asian central banks, dealers said.
*Dollar rose as high as around 114.93 yen in early trade, but offers from Japanese investors above 115 yen also detected.
*Downside solid after Japanese and U.S. officials downplayed trade friction. *The remarks on Thursday showed a reluctance to see dollar below 110 yen, said a senior Japanese bank dealer.
*"Personally, as a dealer, I wanted to see the dollar fall below 110 yen, but the Japanese government showed a strong will to protect that level," he added.
*He said a dollar fall below 110 yen would have opened way for large dollar losses by inducing stop-loss sales orders.
*Such falls would cause heavy losses to some financially weak Japanese institutions and the Finance Ministry did not want to see them in deeper trouble.
*"So there may be even a chance of BOJ dollar-buying intervention if the dollar looks like falling below that point again," the dealer said.
*Dollar fell after earlier edging up on short-covering and purchases by Japanese investors.
*Dealers said dollar's upside remains heavy near 115 yen, with exporter offers around that level.
*Mark/yen sales, possibly by overseas operators, indirectly weighing on dollar/yen, a trust bank dealer said.
*Talk of bids from public funds and pension funds on downside, with dollar support seen near 113.60 yen.
